small_guidance:
- The conv-transpose GEMM uses weight layout (IC, OC, KH, KW) with non-contiguous loads along the K axis (stride KH*KW between IC rows). Pre-permute weight once at init to (IC, KH, KW, OC) contiguous so `w_off = (ic*KH*KW + kh*KW + kw)*OC + oc` gives coalesced loads along BLOCK_N; this should materially cut the GEMM bandwidth.
- Add larger autotune configs (BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3) and a BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128 variant; current best may be picking a small tile. Also key autotune on (OH, OW) so the chosen tile matches the 256x256 output spatial size.
- In `min_sum_gelu_bias_kernel`, BLOCK_OC=128 already covers OC=128 in one pass — drop the inner c_start loop (single load of [OC, BLOCK_H]) and increase BLOCK_H to 64 to halve the outer loop trip count; also launch grid as (N*OW,) with num_warps=2 since each program is small.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite ConvTranspose2d as a scatter-add (input × kernel outer product scattered into the output grid). For stride=2 the gather formulation has 75% of (kh,kw) pairs invalid per output element, wasting K-loop work; a scatter from input space iterates only valid contributions. One program per (N, IC tile, IH tile, IW tile) computing partial outputs, atomic-add (or pre-allocated zero output + atomic) into output — but better: dispatch one program per (N, oh_block, ow_block) and gather only the valid (kh, kw) subset by precomputing the divisibility pattern, reducing K_total from IC*KH*KW=576 to IC*ceil(KH/SH)*ceil(KW/SW)=64 effective taps.
- Fuse the channel-min directly into the conv-transpose epilogue: instead of materializing the (N, OC=128, 256, 256) tensor (~2 GB traffic), have each conv program compute its OC tile's contribution and reduce across OC via a second pass or atomicMin into a (N, 1, OH, OW) buffer; the downstream sum/GELU/bias then reads a 128× smaller tensor. This removes the dominant memory traffic.
- Alternatively, since the final output is only (N, 1, 1, OW), build a single persistent kernel per (N, ow): it iterates oh, and for each oh computes min over oc of the conv-transpose output at (n, oc, oh, ow), accumulating into the row sum — avoids ever writing the full conv tensor. Each (n, ow) program does ~OH*OC*IC*KH*KW/SH/SW work but reads input only, writes one scalar.
